renders._yaml:
- component: card
  id: sequences_total
  title: Sequences kept
  description: |-
    The hero number is the total count of sequences in the files after filtering, and the box shows how many each file holds. It answers how much sequence the later steps receive.
    How to read: a total far below what you started with means the filter was strict, so compare with the before stage in the table. A box with a long tail marks a few files that hold most of the sequences.
    Source: https://telatin.github.io/seqfu2/tools/stats.html
  column: sequences
  aggregation: sum
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  filter_expr: col('stage') != 'before'
  caption: sequences per file, with quartiles
  headline: true

- component: card
  id: mean_length
  title: Mean sequence length
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median over files of their mean sequence length, and the box shows the quartiles. It answers whether the files hold sequences of a similar size.
    How to read: a tight box means uniform files. A wide box mixes short and long sequences, for instance reads with assemblies, so compare it with the N50.
  column: mean_length
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  filter_expr: col('stage') != 'before'
  caption: median, with quartiles

- component: card
  id: n50_length
  title: N50 length
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median over files of their N50, the length such that sequences at least that long hold half of the bases, and the box shows the quartiles. It answers how contiguous the sequences are.
    How to read: a high N50 means most bases sit in long sequences. An N50 far above the mean length shows a few long sequences carry the file, and one near it shows uniform sequences.
    Source: https://telatin.github.io/seqfu2/tools/stats.html and https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/N50,_L50,_and_related_statistics
  column: n50
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  filter_expr: col('stage') != 'before'
  caption: median, with quartiles

- component: figure
  title: Sequences per file by stage
  description: |-
    Each bar is the number of sequences in one file, with the stages (before and after filtering) side by side. It answers how many sequences each filtering step removed.
    How to read: equal bars mean the filter removed nothing from that file. A much shorter after bar marks a file the filter cut down, so open the table to see its lengths.
  visu_type: bar
  dict_kwargs:
    x: sample
    y: sequences
    color: stage
    barmode: group
    labels:
      sample: Sample
      sequences: Sequences
      stage: Stage

- component: table
  title: Sequence file statistics
  description: |-
    Each row is a summarised file: its sample and stage, the sequence count, the total length, the mean, minimum and maximum length, N50, N75, N90 and auN. It answers the exact length statistics behind every other tile.
    How to read: filter by stage to compare before and after, and sort by N50 to find the most fragmented files.
    Note: SeqFu before version 1.22.1 calculated auN incorrectly, so compare auN only between runs of one version.
    Source: https://telatin.github.io/seqfu2/tools/stats.html
